title: ANALYSIS OF EFFECTIVENESS OF NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY IN THE TREATMENT OF LOCALLY ADVANCED COLON CANCER.
official: ANALYSIS OF EFFECTIVENESS OF NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY IN THE TREATMENT OF LOCALLY ADVANCED COLON CANCER.
summary: Main objective: To determine if the proposed treatment with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, surgery and complementary chemotherapy increases Disease-Free Survival (DFS) at 2 years postoperatively, compared to the standard treatment, surgery and complementary chemotherapy.

interventions.name: Oxaliplatin Hospira 5 mg/ml concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Histological confirmation of colon adenocarcinoma.
2. Radiologically resectable disease.
3. Who are going to undergo elective surgery with curative intent (R0).
4. Patients of both sexes aged over 18 years.
5. Good general condition of the patient (Karnofsky>60% or ECOG<2).
6. Analysis at the time of inclusion with hemoglobin levels >10 g/dL; Leukocytes >3.0 109/L, Platelets > 100,000, Glomerular Filtration >50 ml/min and Total Bilirubin <25 micromol/l.
7. Absence of contraindication for chemotherapy.
8. Acceptance and signing of the Informed Consent.
9. Radiological signs, evaluated by CT, of T4 or T3 tumor infiltration >5 mm of transmural invasion.
10. With or without lymph node involvement by CT.
11. Without metastatic involvement in other organs (M0).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Significant comorbidity, uncontrolled angina or history of acute myocardial infarction in the last 6 months.
2. Refusal to participate or give written consent
3. Inability, at the discretion of the researcher, to understand the purpose of the study or comply with its procedures.
4. Personal history of another neoplasm in the last 5 years, except for melanoma.
5. Uncontrolled infection
6. Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
7. Peripheral neuropathy > grade 1.
8. Rectal cancer (< 15 cm from the anal verge or below the peritoneal reflection).
9. Presence of distant metastasis or peritoneal carcinomatosis.
10. Intestinal obstruction.
11. Existence of microsatellite instability
